sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: renewal windows, expiration rules, late-renewal tiers, placard types, address types, indicator documents and boating rules
Confusable pairs among the indicator, placard, renewal and amendment rules, followed by continuation facts the main list did not hold; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A03
A license expired between 180 days and five years needs a knowledge exam and vision screening on renewal, while one expired five years or more also needs a driving skills exam. [A03]
Why it matters: group late renewal; confusable middle tier versus long-expired tier.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A03
A citizen or permanent resident may renew a license or ID card as early as 24 months ahead, but a learner's permit or a lawful temporary resident's credential only 30 days ahead. [A03]
Why it matters: group renewal windows; confusable early-renewal limits.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A03
A probationary license ends at 21 years and 30 days, whereas every other credential runs out at midnight on the holder's birthday. [A03]
Why it matters: group expiration; confusable probationary versus standard expiry.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A02
A permanent placard is free and open-ended, while a temporary placard has a fee and lasts at most one year. [A02]
Why it matters: group placards; confusable permanent versus temporary.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A04
A principal address change needs a branch visit with documents within 30 days, while a mailing address change can be done online, at a kiosk or at a branch. [A04]
Why it matters: group amendments; confusable principal versus mailing address.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A01
An active-duty indicator is backed by a current Common Access Card, a veteran indicator by a DD 214, and a veteran spouse indicator by discharge proof plus marriage and death certificates. [A01]
Why it matters: group indicators; confusable documents by indicator.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A01
An adult's donor declaration cannot be overridden by family, while a minor's declaration depends on a parent or guardian consenting at the time of death. [A01]
Why it matters: group organ donation; confusable adult versus minor donor.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A02
Indiana residents on boundary waters must carry an Indiana license, while out-of-state residents need one only on an Indiana embayment, river or stream. [A02]
Why it matters: group watercraft; confusable resident versus non-resident boaters.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A01
A person aged 15 or older can run a boat over 10 horsepower without a driver's license after an approved boater course, but someone under 15 cannot run one at all. [A01]
Why it matters: group watercraft; confusable fifteen-plus versus under fifteen.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A03
The knowledge exam at renewal is triggered by six or more active points for drivers aged 21 or older. [A03]
Why it matters: group renewal; link to points chapter.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A04
Online replacement is capped at 10 times, after which the holder must replace the credential at a BMV branch. [A04]
Why it matters: group replacement; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R12 | anchor: A04
If your Indiana license, permit or ID card is not expired, the manual says the SSA card replacement can be done online at no cost. [A04]
Why it matters: group name change; scope note as printed.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-R13 | anchor: A03
For chauffeur and public passenger chauffeur licenses, the manual sends readers to the For-Hire Endorsement section of Chapter 2 for renewal, amendment and replacement details. [A03]
Why it matters: group renewal; scope note for-hire.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-R14 | anchor: A02
A company empowered by the state or a political subdivision to run transportation or facility programs for people with physical disabilities may apply for a placard. [A02]
Why it matters: group placards; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-R15 | anchor: A03
Credential expiration dates differ for residents with temporary lawful status. [A03]
Why it matters: group expiration; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0024]
